newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse inches up, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse inches up, seen extending gains.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell in stable turnover on Wednesday but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts expected the bourse to rise further as certain stocks still seemed a good bargain and might create new demand.
Some analysts said the market trading at 16 times historic earnings seemed fairly valued but earnings growth prospects made prices of several stocks look more attractive.

"As far as emerging markets are concerned a P/E of 16 is not bad, but investors pay even greater attention to earnings forecasts, which are good," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

But analysts said some food sector stocks and computer makers, which rose significantly in January, looked overvalued with average P/E in the food sector of 23.6 and Optimus trading at 31.9 times historic earnings.
Analysts said the bourse seemed unruffled by the resignation of Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko but said investors would be watching carefully the moves of his successor Marek Belka.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.3 percent, to 16,528.9, and turnover was virtually flat at 180.7 million zlotys on both markets with 35 issues falling, 33 rising and 19 flat.
Some analysts saw the WIG index hitting new records and piercing psychological resistance at 17,000 this week or next.
Rafako surged 9.7 percent on a newspaper report that it had finished works on a contract possibly worth about $30 million, traders said.
Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) extended Tuesday's loss, falling 5.4 percent in profit-taking after its Monday's debut 65.5 percent higher than its issue price of 29 zlotys.
Shares rose in continuous trade in 12-million-zloty turnover with the WIG 20 index up 0.9 percent to 1,699.9 points.
